markdown:
# Rapid Evidence Synthesis: senolytics and healthspan

- Topic: senolytics and healthspan
- Domain: longevity
- Criteria: human studies only safety 2020+

## Abstract

This draft synthesizes public-index evidence on senolytics and healthspan for the longevity domain. The run retained 4 evidence receipts spanning 2018 to 2024, with 2 review-like items and 2 primary-study items.

## Research Question

This draft examines rapamycin and anti-aging outcomes [1] with a cautious evidence frame suitable for readable output. This synthesis specifically examines the available public-index evidence for the longevity domain, considering the quality, recency, and directness of the retained receipts, to determine whether the current literature supports actionable conclusions for practitioners and researchers.

## Search Summary

Public literature sources were queried with scoped variants and the bundle was reduced to the most relevant retained receipts.

## Evidence Landscape

The retained evidence is review-led and should be interpreted conservatively rather than as final clinical proof.

## Key Findings

The strongest signal is directional support [1] with uncertainty driven by heterogeneous designs and incomplete replication.

## Limitations

This remains a rapid synthesis of indexed evidence rather than a full systematic review with exhaustive full-text screening.

## Gaps Identified

This section draws on 4 retained evidence receipts (2 review, 2 primary) queried on 2026-04-20 via 3 scoped search strings.

## Conclusion

Rapamycin remains decision-relevant [1], but claims should stay inside the limits of the retained evidence bundle.

## Sources

[1] Senolytics in older adults: safety review (2024), review — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2/
[2] Senolytics in mice improve healthspan (2024), primary — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3/
[3] Senolytic efficacy in human healthspan trials (2023), primary — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/5/
